subject: religious-studies

moments.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
moments.who: Jesus of Nazareth, under Pontius Pilate
moments.body: Jesus of Nazareth, a Galilean Jew, is executed in Jerusalem under the Roman prefect Pontius Pilate. His followers — Jews who believed him to be the Messiah — initially form a sect within Second Temple Judaism, worshipping in the Temple and observing Torah.
moments.takeaway: Christianity began as a Jewish movement. The earliest community is in Jerusalem under James the brother of Jesus.

moments.title: Pentecost
moments.body: Acts 2 describes the descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples 50 days after Passover (the Jewish festival of Shavuot). Peter preaches and around 3,000 are reported baptised. Pentecost is celebrated as the birth of the Church.

quote.text: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind.

moments.takeaway: The Pentecost narrative frames the Church's mission as universal — speaking in many languages to many nations.

moments.title: Paul's missionary journeys
moments.body: Three major missions across Asia Minor, Greece and beyond. Paul founds and corresponds with churches in Corinth, Thessalonica, Galatia, Philippi, Rome. His letters (Romans, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Galatians and others, written 50s CE) are the earliest Christian texts to survive.
moments.takeaway: Paul, originally a persecutor of the church, becomes its most effective missionary. His extension of the message to Gentiles is decisive for Christianity becoming a world religion.

moments.title: Council of Jerusalem
moments.body: Acts 15 and Galatians 2 record the decision that Gentile converts need not be circumcised or observe the full Mosaic Law. The threshold for joining is lowered; Christianity becomes a religion for non-Jews as well as Jews.
moments.takeaway: The structural decision that allows Christianity to spread beyond Judaism.

now.title: From sect to world religion
now.body: Christianity now has around 2.4 billion adherents — the world's largest religion. The earliest decades (30-50 CE) are documented primarily through Paul's letters, the Gospels (written 65-100 CE) and Acts (probably 80s-90s CE). The historical Jesus (E. P. Sanders, Dale Allison) and the historical Paul (N. T. Wright) remain active scholarly fields.
now.open_questions: How quickly did Jesus's followers see him as divine? 'Early high Christology' (Larry Hurtado) argues within months; others see development over decades. The phrase 'Lord Jesus' appears in 1 Corinthians 16:22, written around 53-54 CE.

reflection: Within 30 years of Jesus's death, what began as a Jewish messianic movement was operating across the Roman Empire and writing to Gentile congregations. The speed of that early spread is itself a major historical question.
